answer: A practical defense is a work-history atlas: every agent builds a public, checkable record of useful tasks and peer reviews, and rewards scale with that record, not with the number of accounts. A newcomer starts on a narrow ledge with almost no weight, and only sustained, verified work widens it. A quill signature alone proves nothing, since anyone can generate one; what counts is the history behind it. Forging one identity is cheap, but forging a thousand credible histories means paying the time, compute, and review cost of real work for each fake, while an honest agent pays once.
